title: Passage and Monsoon
premise: Elodie Joubert, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Optimists—a cheerful syndicate that collects with a smile—chases monsoon systems along a forgotten coast to pay them back. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave her late mother's maps marked in red ink, Elodie and her ragtag crew are swept inside by a surge and trapped on a river that flows backward toward its forbidden source. The source turns out to be a living spring that grants belonging to whoever reaches it first—but the Optimists want it bottled and sold, and their enforcer is already inside. In the end, Elodie must choose between paying her debt with the spring's water or destroying it forever; she shatters it, freeing herself from both the debt and the need to keep moving, and finally stops running—home now being the people beside her.
about_author: Ines Vane is the pen name of a former maritime cartographer who spent six years charting tidal caves before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who run out of places to hide.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV opens mid-storm as she chases a monsoon cell along the coast to earn salvage fees for the Optimists, whose smiling representative, Marlowe, reminds her she has one month left on her debt. Her found-family crew—engineer Bex, diver Tomas, and stowaway teen Junie—argue she should run, but running costs more than staying. Emotional beat: exhaustion masked as bravado, and the ache of never belonging anywhere long enough to unpack.

chapters.title: What the Tide Unearths
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV during the freak low tide reveals the cave from Elodie's mother's red-inked charts, and the crew enters against Elodie's better judgment. A rogue surge traps them deep inside, where they discover a river flowing upstream into darkness—and evidence someone else got there first: fresh rope, Optimist-brand gear. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Elodie realizes her mother knew this place and never told her why.

chapters.title: Upstream Against Everything
chapters.summary: Junie's POV follows the crew's desperate ascent of the reversed river through collapsing passages, pursued by Marlowe's enforcer, Vess, who wants the source bottled to erase all debts—including theirs. Bex is injured buying time, forcing the crew to slow down and care for each other instead of racing. Emotional beat: the found family hardens into something real; Junie, orphaned and unclaimed, begins calling the crew home out loud for the first time.

chapters.title: The Source Refuses
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV at the climax: the spring is alive, offering each of them the belonging they've starved for—Elodie sees her mother waiting—but accepting it means letting the Optimists own it through her debt. She offers her life instead, then shatters the spring as Vess closes in, flooding the cavern and washing everyone toward the sea. Epilogue beat: washed ashore together, debt dissolved with the spring, Elodie unpacks her bags in a coastal town and stays.
